When on, an Uzbek phone number is read as \"+998. 94. 773. 99. 10.\": a pause after each group, and each group read as a number. When off, the number is read in the usual way.

When on, abbreviations of length, weight, volume, time and temperature are read as Uzbek words: “5 kg” is read “besh kilogramm”, “20 °C” is read “yigirma daraja”. When off, the abbreviation is not spoken; only the number is read.
When on, physical units are read as words: “220 V” is read “ikki yuz yigirma volt”, “50 Hz” is read “ellik gers”, also N, J, W, A, Pa. When off, the abbreviation is not spoken.
When on, symbols are read as words: “2+3=5” is read “ikki plyus uch teng besh”, also ×, ÷, √, π, ≤, ≥, x², sin, cos and Greek letters. When off, the symbols are not spoken.
When on, abbreviations such as “250 MB”, “100 Mbit/s” and “1080 px” are read as Uzbek words (“ikki yuz ellik megabayt”). When off, the abbreviation is not spoken.
Step aside when another screen reader starts

When on, if another screen reader (such as TalkBack) starts, O\'zbegim goes into standby (it stops reading and releases gestures) and tells you. When the other screen reader is turned off, O\'zbegim starts again by itself.

Each line: word=pronunciation (for example: settings=setings). Per app: package|word=pronunciation. A line starting with # is a comment. A word that was read wrongly can also be added from the menu: open the menu (tap once with three fingers, or swipe down then right) and choose “Add a word to the pronunciation dictionary”.
Each line: full_id=label (for example: com.app:id/send=Send). If you focus an unlabeled element and swipe left, then down, its identifier is added here.

Each line: package=verbosity:short;echo:off;bridge:off;notify:off;chat:on;sensitive:on. verbosity: short, normal or full. The rest: on or off. sensitive:on is for private apps (bank, payments): the black box is not recorded, chat mode and copying are turned off.

Uzbek voices are installed through RHVoice: Islom, Dilnavoz and Sevinch. Install RHVoice first, download the Uzbek voice inside it, then come back here and choose the voice. Voice packs of other speech engines installed on the phone can also be used: choose an engine below. The list is built from the voices the engine provides.
License: the three RHVoice voices are distributed under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, that is, for non-commercial use only. For this reason they are not included in the app.

resources.string: For Microsoft voices, translation and AI descriptions. Off by default: nothing is sent to the network until you turn it on.

If you turn it on: when a Microsoft voice is chosen, the text being spoken is sent to the Microsoft Azure server. When you perform the translate or screen description gesture, the focused text or the screen image is sent to the server of the chosen AI service (Gemini, ChatGPT, Claude or another service you specify). Nothing is sent in banking and other private apps, nor for passwords and codes. Keys are stored encrypted on the device. If the network drops, the voice returns to the local engine.
Microsoft voices (online): need the internet and an Azure Speech key (Settings, Online features). Quality: 48 kHz. If the network drops, the voice switches to the local engine automatically.

Xiaomi, Redmi, POCO: set the app’s battery mode to “No restrictions” and allow auto-start, otherwise the system may stop the service.
Huawei and Honor: switch the app to manual management (auto-launch and background activity turned on). If there are no Google services, install RHVoice for an Uzbek voice.
OPPO, Realme, OnePlus: turn off battery optimization and allow auto-start.
vivo, iQOO: allow background activity and turn off the high power consumption restriction.
Samsung: in the battery settings do not add O‘zbegim to the list of sleeping apps. Samsung’s own screen reader is called Voice Assistant.
Tecno, Infinix, itel: allow auto-start in the phone manager and turn off the battery restriction.

resources.string: When on, text is read with pauses and emphasis that follow the punctuation.
